items.title: Show HN: DeepSeek V3 in ~200 lines of pure Jax
items.body:
The architecture from the DeepSeek-V3 technical report in 190 lines of pure JAX, pretrained from scratch on a MacBook Air on public-domain detective fiction.

No Flax, no Equinox, no PyTorch. Params are plain dicts of arrays and every part of the model is a function you can read top to bottom in deepseek_v3.py.

Read the write-up: DeepSeek V3 in 190 lines of pure JAX, with diagrams, the code explained piece by piece, and the results.

One run of the default config on a MacBook Air M5 (24 GB):

With balancing on and off, validation loss at step 2000 was the same (3.921 vs 3.923). The bias evens out the experts without costing anything, which is the paper's claim.

Its own words, from the prompt "The fog came in off the":

The fog came in off the bay, and the great trees were spreading and the stars were shining.

This is an architecture demo, not a strong language model. See the write-up for what worked, what didn't, and what's missing.

The v1.0 release has the exact checkpoint and data from the published run. After installing (step 1):

mkdir -p data runs/main curl -L -o runs/main/ckpt.pkl https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/ckpt.pkl # 138 MB curl -L -o data/tokenizer.json https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/tokenizer.json .venv/bin/python sample.py --prompt "The fog came in off the" --num 3

The checkpoint is a Python pickle, which can run code when loaded. Only load checkpoints from sources you trust.

You need an Apple Silicon Mac, Python 3.12 and uv. The published run used 24 GB of memory. No Mac? See Running on CPU.

git clone https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax.git && cd deepseek-v3-jax uv venv -p 3.12 .venv uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt

Every version in requirements.txt is pinned. jax-metal 0.1.1 only works with jax==0.4.34, so don't upgrade JAX.

JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/pytest tests.py -q # 39 passed .venv/bin/python smoke_metal.py # optional: what jax-metal supports on your Mac

In smoke_metal.py, "grad through 2-axis contraction" fails on jax-metal 0.1.1. That's expected, and the model is written to avoid it.

.venv/bin/python prepare_data.py

This downloads the 207 books in sources.txt (~120 MB, about 7 minutes), cleans them, trains an 8,192-token BPE tokenizer and writes data/train.bin, data/val.bin and data/tokenizer.json. It should print:

train: 211 docs, 83.4M chars, 21.69M tokens val: 4 docs, 1.1M chars, 0.30M tokens

The published run's data had these hashes:

shasum -a 256 data/train.bin data/val.bin data/tokenizer.json

d37aca97e707bb81b6e4d266cc1adfd1f3e3556457c6eb724e495118a734e0bb data/train.bin b7ac285b115e6793b5d36aa5b4bc6e81a5fccfc7af0908a306d3828ebca9c31c data/val.bin c5a142b4006a967c880dda44ad792719d53c16d947da3b6c2332d6132d9967cc data/tokenizer.json

You will most likely get different hashes. The Hammett books are pinned to exact Standard Ebooks commits and come out identical, but Project Gutenberg files can't be pinned, and Gutenberg has since re-issued 28 of the 203 books with small edits (mostly accents stripped, like "José" → "Jose"). The token counts come out the same, so training should behave the same.

To train on the exact same bytes, skip prepare_data.py and download the published data instead:

mkdir -p data for f in train.bin val.bin tokenizer.json; do curl -L -o data/$f https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/$f; done shasum -a 256 data/*.bin data/tokenizer.json # should match the hashes above

.venv/bin/python train.py # the main run: 12k steps, ~2.6 h .venv/bin/python train.py --steps 2000 --out runs/bias_on # balancing ablation, with the bias .venv/bin/python train.py --steps 2000 --out runs/bias_off --no-bias # ...and without it

Each run writes metrics.jsonl (loss, validation loss, per-expert load, biases, tokens/s) and ckpt.pkl (saved at every evaluation) into its --out folder, which defaults to runs/main. Seeds are fixed, but GPU math on Metal isn't bit-for-bit deterministic, so expect your numbers to land close to the ones above rather than match them exactly.

.venv/bin/python sample.py --prompt "The fog came in off the" --num 3

Defaults: temperature 0.8, top-k 50, 300 new tokens per sample (--temp, --top-k, --n).

.venv/bin/python plots.py # needs runs/main, runs/bias_on, runs/bias_off JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/python charts.py # the rest of the write-up's charts

Both write into post/figures/.

To redraw the figures without training, download the logs from the release: metrics-main.jsonl, metrics-bias_on.jsonl and metrics-bias_off.jsonl go into runs/main/, runs/bias_on/ and runs/bias_off/ as metrics.jsonl. charts.py also needs the checkpoint and the data.

Everything runs without jax-metal. It's much slower, so use the smaller config:

JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/python train.py --config small

--config small (4 layers, 8 experts, top-2, 128-token context) is meant for 8–16 GB Macs too. It has only been checked for a couple of steps, not trained to the end.

"190 lines" counts the non-blank, non-comment lines of deepseek_v3.py after its docstring:

tail -n +5 deepseek_v3.py | grep -cvE '^\s*(#|$)' # 190

Dense MoE compute. Every expert runs on every token and the unpicked ones are zeroed. The routing math is exact, but there's no sparse dispatch or expert parallelism.

No weight absorption in MLA. The latent is decompressed explicitly, which is easier to read and slower at inference.

Not included: FP8 training, DualPipe, node-limited routing, YaRN context extension, and any post-training.

Scale. 36.2M parameters vs 671B, 6 layers vs 61, a 256-token context vs 128K.

All training text is public domain in the United States: Dashiell Hammett's Red Harvest, The Dain Curse, The Maltese Falcon and Continental Op stories (CC0 editions from Standard Ebooks), plus about 200 detective and crime novels from Project Gutenberg. Every source is listed in sources.txt. Public-domain status outside the US may differ.

DeepSeek-AI, DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report, 2024.

Code: MIT. The training text is public domain in the US (see above).
items.body_ko:
DeepSeek-V3 기술 보고서의 아키텍처를 순수 JAX 190줄로 구현했으며, MacBook Air에서 공개 도메인 탐정 소설을 사용하여 처음부터 사전 학습했습니다.

Flax, Equinox, PyTorch는 사용하지 않았습니다. 매개변수는 배열의 일반 딕셔너리이며 모델의 모든 부분은 deepseek_v3.py에서 위에서 아래로 읽을 수 있는 함수입니다.

설명 글 읽어보기: 다이어그램, 조각별 코드 설명 및 결과가 포함된 순수 JAX 190줄의 DeepSeek V3.

MacBook Air M5 (24 GB)에서 기본 구성을 한 번 실행한 결과:

밸런싱을 켜고 껐을 때, 2000단계에서의 검증 손실은 동일했습니다 (3.921 대 3.923). 바이어스는 아무런 비용 없이 전문가를 고르게 만들었는데, 이는 논문의 주장입니다.

프롬프트 "안개가 밀려왔다"에서 모델이 생성한 단어:

안개가 만에서 밀려왔고, 거대한 나무들이 퍼져 있었고 별들이 빛나고 있었다.

이것은 아키텍처 데모이며 강력한 언어 모델이 아닙니다. 어떤 점이 효과가 있었고, 어떤 점이 없었으며, 어떤 점이 부족한지에 대해서는 설명 글을 참조하세요.

v1.0 릴리스에는 게시된 실행의 정확한 체크포인트와 데이터가 포함되어 있습니다. (1단계) 설치 후:

mkdir -p data runs/main curl -L -o runs/main/ckpt.pkl https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/ckpt.pkl # 138 MB curl -L -o data/tokenizer.json https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/tokenizer.json .venv/bin/python sample.py --prompt "The fog came in off the" --num 3

체크포인트는 로드할 때 코드를 실행할 수 있는 Python pickle입니다. 신뢰할 수 있는 소스의 체크포인트만 로드하세요.

Apple Silicon Mac, Python 3.12, uv가 필요합니다. 게시된 실행은 24GB의 메모리를 사용했습니다. Mac이 없나요? CPU에서 실행하기를 참조하세요.

git clone https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax.git && cd deepseek-v3-jax uv venv -p 3.12 .venv uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt

requirements.txt의 모든 버전은 고정되어 있습니다. jax-metal 0.1.1은 jax==0.4.34에서만 작동하므로 JAX를 업그레이드하지 마세요.

JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/pytest tests.py -q # 39 passed .venv/bin/python smoke_metal.py # optional: what jax-metal supports on your Mac

smoke_metal.py에서 "grad through 2-axis contraction"은 jax-metal 0.1.1에서 실패합니다. 이는 예상된 결과이며, 모델은 이를 피하도록 작성되었습니다.

.venv/bin/python prepare_data.py

이것은 sources.txt에 있는 207권의 책(~120MB, 약 7분)을 다운로드하고, 정리하고, 8,192 토큰 BPE 토크나이저를 훈련하고 data/train.bin, data/val.bin, data/tokenizer.json을 작성합니다. 다음과 같이 출력되어야 합니다:

train: 211 docs, 83.4M chars, 21.69M tokens val: 4 docs, 1.1M chars, 0.30M tokens

게시된 실행의 데이터는 다음과 같은 해시를 가졌습니다:

shasum -a 256 data/train.bin data/val.bin data/tokenizer.json

d37aca97e707bb81b6e4d266cc1adfd1f3e3556457c6eb724e495118a734e0bb data/train.bin b7ac285b115e6793b5d36aa5b4bc6e81a5fccfc7af0908a306d3828ebca9c31c data/val.bin c5a142b4006a967c880dda44ad792719d53c16d947da3b6c2332d6132d9967cc data/tokenizer.json

대부분의 경우 다른 해시를 얻게 될 것입니다. Hammett의 책은 정확한 Standard Ebooks 커밋에 고정되어 동일하게 나오지만, Project Gutenberg 파일은 고정할 수 없으며, Gutenberg는 이후 203권 중 28권을 작은 편집(대부분 "José" → "Jose"와 같이 악센트가 제거됨)으로 재발행했습니다. 토큰 수는 동일하게 나오므로 훈련은 동일하게 작동해야 합니다.

정확히 동일한 바이트로 훈련하려면 prepare_data.py를 건너뛰고 대신 게시된 데이터를 다운로드하세요:

mkdir -p data for f in train.bin val.bin tokenizer.json; do curl -L -o data/$f https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/$f; done shasum -a 256 data/*.bin data/tokenizer.json # should match the hashes above

.venv/bin/python train.py # the main run: 12k steps, ~2.6 h .venv/bin/python train.py --steps 2000 --out runs/bias_on # balancing ablation, with the bias .venv/bin/python train.py --steps 2000 --out runs/bias_off --no-bias # ...and without it

각 실행은 metrics.jsonl (손실, 검증 손실, 전문가별 로드, 바이어스, 토큰/초)와 ckpt.pkl (모든 평가 시 저장됨)을 해당 --out 폴더에 작성하며, 기본값은 runs/main입니다. 시드는 고정되어 있지만, Metal의 GPU 계산은 비트 단위로 결정론적이지 않으므로, 숫자가 위의 숫자와 정확히 일치하기보다는 비슷하게 나올 것으로 예상하세요.

.venv/bin/python sample.py --prompt "The fog came in off the" --num 3

기본값: temperature 0.8, top-k 50, 샘플당 300개의 새 토큰 (--temp, --top-k, --n).

.venv/bin/python plots.py # needs runs/main, runs/bias_on, runs/bias_off JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/python charts.py # the rest of the write-up's charts

둘 다 post/figures/에 작성됩니다.

훈련 없이 그림을 다시 그리려면 릴리스에서 로그를 다운로드하세요: metrics-main.jsonl, metrics-bias_on.jsonl 및 metrics-bias_off.jsonl은 각각 runs/main/, runs/bias_on/ 및 runs/bias_off/에 metrics.jsonl로 들어갑니다. charts.py는 체크포인트와 데이터도 필요합니다.

jax-metal 없이 모든 것이 실행됩니다. 훨씬 느리므로 더 작은 구성을 사용하세요:

JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/python train.py --config small

--config small (4 레이어, 8 전문가, top-2, 128 토큰 컨텍스트)은 8–16 GB Mac에도 적합합니다. 몇 단계만 확인되었으며 끝까지 훈련되지는 않았습니다.

"190줄"은 deepseek_v3.py의 독스트링 다음의 비어 있지 않고 주석이 아닌 줄을 계산합니다:

tail -n +5 deepseek_v3.py | grep -cvE '^\s*(#|$)' # 190

Dense MoE 계산. 모든 전문가는 모든 토큰에서 실행되며 선택되지 않은 토큰은 0으로 처리됩니다. 라우팅 계산은 정확하지만, 희소 디스패치나 전문가 병렬 처리는 없습니다.

MLA에 가중치 흡수 없음. 잠재 변수는 명시적으로 압축 해제되며, 이는 읽기 쉽지만 추론 시 느립니다.

포함되지 않음: FP8 훈련, DualPipe, 노드 제한 라우팅, YaRN 컨텍스트 확장 및 사후 훈련.

규모. 36.2M 매개변수 대 671B, 6 레이어 대 61, 256 토큰 컨텍스트 대 128K.

모든 훈련 텍스트는 미국에서 공개 도메인입니다: Dashiell Hammett의 Red Harvest, The Dain Curse, The Maltese Falcon 및 Continental Op 이야기 (Standard Ebooks의 CC0 에디션)와 Project Gutenberg의 약 200권의 탐정 및 범죄 소설. 모든 출처는 sources.txt에 나열되어 있습니다. 공개 도메인 통계

items.title: Show HN: Agweb – a browser for agents that stays out of your way
items.body:
A browser for coding agents on macOS, built on WebKit (Safari's engine). I run several coding agents at once, and Playwright's Chrome windows kept stealing my keyboard, while headless browsers got blocked by some sites and left me guessing what went wrong. agweb is one window that never takes focus: agents drive it from the shell with agweb, a playwright-cli-style command, and you watch them all live.

Idle tabs are suspended: on my Mac five open pages sit at 0% CPU, where Chrome's GPU process kept five to seven cores busy.

Never steals focus. No window comes to the front, nothing pops up. Dialogs, changing tabs, file pickers and downloads are answered in code.

You can always see it. The dashboard (⌘D) shows every tab of every agent at once, live, with each agent's last command. And it is always a real window: some sites block headless browsers, and headless leaves you guessing what went wrong.

Many agents at once. Each agent works in its own workspace with its own tabs, grouped by agent in the sidebar.

Log in once. A named profile (-p work) keeps its logins and is shared by every agent using it, at the same time.

Light. Idle tabs are throttled and then suspended, so open pages cost almost nothing once nobody uses them.

Acts like a person. Clicks and keys are native macOS events, and the pointer moves like a hand, so hover menus and drag-and-drop work.

Made for agents. Snapshots give each element a ref that lasts while it is on the page. snapshot --diff and find show only what matters, and every action reports what it changed.

Passwords stay out of the transcript. fill --secret-cmd 'pass show site' types a secret the agent never sees in replies. 1Password and Bitwarden CLIs work too.

No ads. Ads and trackers are blocked with uBlock Origin's lists, which agweb downloads every 4 days. An agent testing analytics can turn it off for its own workspace (agweb -w task adblock off).

Demo videos. video-start records a tab to MP4, with the pointer and clicks drawn in.

Needs macOS 26 or later. Download Agweb.dmg from Releases, drag Agweb to Applications and open it. Then:

Help ▸ Install Command Line Tool

Help ▸ Install Agent Skill (for Claude Code and Codex).

Both are links into the app, so they update with it.

To build from source instead (Xcode 26 or later):

./scripts/build.sh build/Agweb.app/Contents/Helpers/agweb install-cli agweb install-skill

agweb -w task open en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebKit # a workspace for this task; starts the app if needed agweb -w task snapshot # the page as a tree with [ref=eN] handles agweb -w task click 'role=button[name="Main menu"]'

The click's reply already says what it did, so the agent needs no second snapshot:

### Changes - navigation "Site" [ref=e2] - - button "Main menu" [ref=e3] + - button "Main menu" [checked] [expanded] [ref=e3] + - list [ref=e1167] + - listitem [ref=e1168] + - link "Main page" [ref=e1169]

agweb help lists every command. Settings (⌘,) has text size, dashboard columns, a CPU and memory readout and the ad blocker switch.

Same commands where possible, so agents already know them; a Playwright name it lacks suggests its own (scroll-to → scroll-into-view). On top:

Replies say what changed: fetches started, lines added or removed, dialogs, popups, downloads, console errors. No snapshot after every step, so far fewer tokens.

Refs last while the element is on the page.

ask hands the tab to you for a login, MFA code or CAPTCHA, without taking focus.

Actions wait for the fetches they caused, so agents rarely sleep.

text returns the page's article as markdown.

Shared logins: agents on one profile run at once; a Chrome profile opens in one browser only.

WebKit only: no Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Playwright and Chrome extensions can't attach, and Chrome-only sites may misbehave.

route mocks fetch and XHR only; requests lists images, scripts and styles by URL only (--static).

The ad blocker can't run uBlock's scripts, so YouTube ads and some "turn off your ad blocker" walls get through.

For what it can't do, use Playwright.

./scripts/selftest.sh runs every command against a local page in a separate instance; swift test runs the unit tests. AGWEB_ROOT=/tmp/dir starts a second instance beside your own that keeps everything in that folder. Defuddle (MIT) is bundled for text.

macOS에서 코딩 에이전트를 위한 브라우저로, WebKit(Safari 엔진)을 기반으로 구축되었습니다. 저는 여러 코딩 에이전트를 동시에 실행하는데, Playwright의 Chrome 창이 계속 키보드 포커스를 뺏어가고, 헤드리스 브라우저는 일부 사이트에서 차단되어 무엇이 문제인지 추측해야 했습니다. agweb은 포커스를 뺏지 않는 하나의 창입니다. 에이전트는 Playwright-CLI 스타일 명령어인 agweb을 사용하여 셸에서 agweb을 구동하고, 사용자는 모든 작업을 실시간으로 볼 수 있습니다.

유휴 탭은 일시 중단됩니다. 제 Mac에서는 5개의 열린 페이지가 CPU 0%를 유지하는 반면, Chrome의 GPU 프로세스는 5~7개의 코어를 계속 사용했습니다.

절대 포커스를 뺏지 않습니다. 어떤 창도 앞으로 나오지 않고, 아무것도 팝업되지 않습니다. 대화 상자, 탭 변경, 파일 선택기 및 다운로드는 코드로 응답됩니다.

항상 볼 수 있습니다. 대시보드(⌘D)는 모든 에이전트의 모든 탭을 실시간으로 동시에 보여주며, 각 에이전트의 마지막 명령어를 함께 표시합니다. 그리고 항상 실제 창입니다. 일부 사이트는 헤드리스 브라우저를 차단하며, 헤드리스는 무엇이 잘못되었는지 추측하게 만듭니다.

동시에 많은 에이전트. 각 에이전트는 고유한 작업 공간에서 자체 탭을 가지고 작동하며, 사이드바에서 에이전트별로 그룹화됩니다.

한 번 로그인. 이름 지정된 프로필(-p work)은 로그인을 유지하고, 이를 사용하는 모든 에이전트가 동시에 공유합니다.

가볍습니다. 유휴 탭은 스로틀링된 다음 일시 중단되므로, 사용되지 않는 열린 페이지는 거의 비용이 들지 않습니다.

사람처럼 작동합니다. 클릭과 키 입력은 네이티브 macOS 이벤트이며, 포인터는 손처럼 움직여 호버 메뉴와 드래그 앤 드롭이 작동합니다.

에이전트를 위해 만들어졌습니다. 스냅샷은 각 요소에 페이지에 있는 동안 지속되는 ref를 부여합니다. snapshot --diff와 find는 중요한 것만 보여주며, 모든 작업은 변경된 사항을 보고합니다.

비밀번호는 스크립트에 남지 않습니다. fill --secret-cmd 'pass show site'는 에이전트가 답장에서 절대 볼 수 없는 비밀을 입력합니다. 1Password 및 Bitwarden CLI도 작동합니다.

광고 없음. 광고와 트래커는 uBlock Origin의 목록으로 차단되며, agweb은 4일마다 이를 다운로드합니다. 분석 테스트 에이전트는 자체 작업 공간(agweb -w task adblock off)에서 이를 끌 수 있습니다.

데모 비디오. video-start는 포인터와 클릭이 그려진 상태로 탭을 MP4로 녹화합니다.

macOS 26 이상이 필요합니다. Releases에서 Agweb.dmg를 다운로드하고, Agweb을 Applications로 드래그한 다음 엽니다. 그런 다음:

Help ▸ Install Command Line Tool

Help ▸ Install Agent Skill (Claude Code 및 Codex용).

두 가지 모두 앱 내 링크이므로 앱과 함께 업데이트됩니다.

대신 소스에서 빌드하려면 (Xcode 26 이상):

./scripts/build.sh build/Agweb.app/Contents/Helpers/agweb install-cli agweb install-skill

agweb -w task open en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebKit # 이 작업을 위한 작업 공간; 필요한 경우 앱 시작 agweb -w task snapshot # [ref=eN] 핸들이 있는 트리 형태의 페이지 agweb -w task click 'role=button[name="Main menu"]'

클릭의 응답에는 이미 수행된 작업이 명시되어 있으므로 에이전트는 두 번째 스냅샷이 필요하지 않습니다.

### Changes - navigation "Site" [ref=e2] - - button "Main menu" [ref=e3] + - button "Main menu" [checked] [expanded] [ref=e3] + - list [ref=e1167] + - listitem [ref=e1168] + - link "Main page" [ref=e1169]

agweb help는 모든 명령어를 나열합니다. Settings (⌘,)에는 텍스트 크기, 대시보드 열, CPU 및 메모리 사용량 표시, 광고 차단기 스위치가 있습니다.

가능한 경우 동일한 명령어를 사용하여 에이전트가 이미 이를 알고 있습니다. Playwright에 없는 이름은 자체적으로 제안합니다 (scroll-to → scroll-into-view). 그 외에:

응답은 변경된 사항을 알려줍니다. 가져오기가 시작되었는지, 줄이 추가되거나 제거되었는지, 대화 상자, 팝업, 다운로드, 콘솔 오류 등입니다. 모든 단계 후에 스냅샷이 없으므로 토큰 수가 훨씬 적습니다.

Refs는 요소가 페이지에 있는 동안 지속됩니다.

ask는 로그인, MFA 코드 또는 CAPTCHA를 위해 포커스를 뺏지 않고 탭을 사용자에게 넘겨줍니다.

Actions는 발생시킨 가져오기를 기다리므로 에이전트는 거의 절전 모드로 들어가지 않습니다.

text는 페이지의 문서를 Markdown으로 반환합니다.

공유 로그인: 하나의 프로필에 있는 에이전트가 동시에 실행됩니다. Chrome 프로필은 하나의 브라우저에서만 열립니다.

WebKit 전용: Chrome DevTools Protocol이 없으므로 Playwright 및 Chrome 확장 프로그램은 연결할 수 없으며, Chrome 전용 사이트가 오작동할 수 있습니다.

route는 fetch 및 XHR만 모의합니다. requests는 URL(--static)로만 이미지, 스크립트 및 스타일을 나열합니다.

광고 차단기는 uBlock의 스크립트를 실행할 수 없으므로 YouTube 광고 및 일부 "광고 차단기를 끄세요" 벽이 통과될 수 있습니다.

할 수 없는 작업은 Playwright를 사용하십시오.

./scripts/selftest.sh는 별도의 인스턴스에서 로컬 페이지에 대해 모든 명령어를 실행합니다. swift test는 단위 테스트를 실행합니다. AGWEB_ROOT=/tmp/dir은 모든 것을 해당 폴더에 보관하는 자신 옆에 두 번째 인스턴스를 시작합니다. Defuddle (MIT)는 텍스트용으로 번들되어 있습니다.

items.title: Open-source AI without Jensen
items.body:
The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a major setback for the US development of an open model ecosystem. Nvidia still has the financial interests in supporting open models, which are to avoid concentration in power among a few customers who would develop their own chips and reduce Nvidia’s profits, but supporting the open ecosystem is a tricky puzzle more than an engineering problem to grind out a solution on.
Nvidia’s business operations are famously extremely dependent on Jensen as an operator, so it is a consensus opinion that there are challenges ahead (or even more high-profile departures through chip-smuggling investigations or plain-old sharks circling more poachable talent). Nvidia’s number one goal is to stabilize the ship, deliver to customers in the next 24 months, and prevent implosion. Open models have been one of Jensen’s more ambitious, founder-style bets. He has been flooding the zone with funding in a way that will very likely dry up.
Interconnects AI is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.

In this period, the open model economy is in its nascency. These are crucial years for establishing use-cases, revenue flow, and motives to continue training the next generation models. I discussed the sensitivity of these early years in my recent talk at Fireworks Forge (slides, recording). The core of the argument is one upside for open models, a reason to be optimistic, and one downside.
The positive case is that the open model economy has correctly latched onto “ownership of intelligence” and enterprise post-training as a crucial lane. What is to be determined is exactly how big the downstream market is.
The downside is that the true long-term benefit of open models, as truly commoditized intelligence, is very far from realization with compute in such short supply. In the near term, where inference startups are also struggling to get enough chips (because Anthropic and OpenAI are buying so much capacity), there’s little margin competition on open-weight models. If open-source models are also served at giant inference margins, as we learned with DeepSeek’s DeepInfer release, they’re far from a commodity. In this paradigm, the closed labs with better economies of scale and integration from model to datacenter and chips will win. I expanded on this challenge in my recent piece on the open model economy.
Together, a lot still needs to go right for open models to be a meaningful economic engine. Jensen’s support, and protection, gave the ecosystem time to figure this out.
Jensen was more than a cheerleader. He would stop a lot of shit from going wrong once early winds were stirring. He was willing to use his power on open models.
There’s a major swell in Democratic government funding towards candidates that want to regulate the AI industry, fostering “safety”. Many of these people feel a need to do something and have general opinions that open models are unsafe, while not being educated on the complexities of their benefits. My biggest near-term worry is sloppy regulation at the state level, followed by national regulation. We’ve been one, strong Chinese open-weight model away from a crisis since this summer. It still holds – especially as we enter a new, turbulent equilibrium of cybersecurity. We have not seen a major hack driven by a popular Chinese open-weight model, but it is a matter of when, not if. We need someone to encourage caution and an ecosystem perspective when the “open-weight hawks” come hunting.
Knocking over the open-source AI domino today is easy — if done, unwinding the downstream concentration of power, reduction in safety research, and stifling of long-term innovation is far harder. On public data, it looks like balancing long-term innovation versus short term risks, but this is due to how horribly hard it is to measure the open model economy (e.g. the most valuable aspects of it run on private infrastructure). It’s a recurring challenge facing the ecosystem and my work.
As a brief aside, the extent to which the media ecosystem is revolving around timing today, rather than exact availability of information, is incredible. All of these Jensen affairs were known, but getting them out at the right time, right after the midterm political swing, took down the king.
The same goes for the Jacob Coxon brouhaha this summer. All of that safety culture around top labs was well known, but the right timing around datacenters and the Overton window made it a national issue. This could very well happen at some point for open model safety, as it tends to be harm, risk, or safety-related narratives that drive the modern media algorithms. I cannot imagine my work on open-science driving such a media cycle, because it will never happen.
Share
The only lasting solution to this is to incubate a truly frontier open model player in the US. For example, I agree completely with Dylan Patel, CEO of SemiAnalysis, on a core problem in the US open model ecosystem. From a recent ChinaTalk + SemiAnalysis emergency podcast:
Jordan Schneider: I do want your guys’ take on just how bad this is, that Jensen’s now off the table for the future of American innovation. And we should talk about open models. I mean, he was the big champion, right? Dylan, you were talking earlier — I still don’t understand quite why someone didn’t just spend a few billion dollars and make something better than Kimi or DeepSeek and open source it.
Dylan Patel: Not that easy. It’s not money, it’s talent, man. All of the most talented people primarily work at Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, and Meta TBD, right? And then those who don’t are split across a hundred different startups. I mean, yes, Thinking Machines has a cracked team, but is Thinking Machines as good as Moonshot? No. Moonshot skill-wise is probably just as good as the US labs. They just have a big deficit in compute and deployment. So I think if we don’t have a scale advantage, then you don’t win. Yes, these smaller labs have spent a lot of money on models. But DeepMind, Grok, Meta have regularly fallen behind the frontier of Chinese labs, and they’re spending more. So it’s not just, oh, spend a few billion dollars and you can make a model that’s better.

The best people for attracting talent are the ones at the front of movements. Jensen helped catalyze this, and on many metrics was still losing. Nemotron has had the right level of ambition and strong people, but it hasn’t delivered to the point of being called “mission accomplished.” The competition here in building leading-edge models is more fierce than most give credit to. Having an organization with billions of dollars, solid people, and good vibes may not get you there. You normally need something special.
It could be the case that Thinking Machines has gotten to maturity in its commitment to open models, with its recent Inkling 2 Small being the best Western open-weight model in a while. Still, it’s far behind Kimi K3.1 Pro and expectations are high for Zhipu’s next GLM update. It’s a better sign that we’re at least having this debate, but the open ecosystem is riddled with questions and answers like this – maybe they can pull it off? On the other side of the equation, closed labs like Anthropic look like some of the greatest businesses ever assembled, which inspires confidence in the longevity of their approach.
Who is Mira going to call when they need to close their next funding round? Supposedly the next round at a $40B valuation is a done deal, but that won’t be enough to keep pace with the closed frontier for long.
The fundamental problem is that the open-weight ecosystem needs someone who will pick up the phone to abate a crisis. There are more challenges ahead. The most likely allies we could turn to are from the hyperscalers, the likes of Zuckerberg, Andy Jassy, or Satya. Gemini 4 Hydrogen in GitHub Copilot. GitHub made the model generally available in Copilot across its app, CLI and VS Code. GitHub
Independent checks: Roboflow's vision bench shows high effort at 29.3s per image, against 51.4s for Argon and 132.3s for Carbon, though Carbon has better detection accuracy (@skalskip92). One 3D-modeling test found Hydrogen more expensive than Argon because it loops on over-verification (@dzhng).

Google's week: Google also shipped two 8th-gen TPUs, Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini Robotics 2.5, AlphaGenome 2 and a Decisions API (@sundarpichai).

MathArena: Gemini 4 Carbon took #1, displacing GPT-6.1 Sol (@j_dekoninck).

Claude Fable 5.2 in Agent Arena. Arena published new results for long coding sessions.
Pricing: API pricing fell from $10/$50 to $8/$40 per 1M input/output tokens (@arena).

Agent Arena: The model ranks #1 at +30.4% net improvement, about 1.6x Opus 5.5. Its lead grows on long tasks, reaching 93% vs 85% no-correction responses at 16+ turns (@arena, turns).

Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Small: The model's open weights are now on the Hub (@ariG23498). It is the #1 US open model in Code Arena WebDev at 1647 (@arena).
NVFP4 training: It uses a native 4-bit forward pass from the first pretraining step through the final RL rollout (blog). The mixed-precision recipe is detailed by @jackcookjack. NVFP4 is stored in 3.6x fewer bits than BF16 and runs up to 6x faster on GB300 (quote).

Inference detail: A width-4 short convolution requires a rolling 3-token cache per layer alongside the KV cache (@andrew_n_carr).

ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview (Baidu): The model has 280B total and 14B active parameters, a 1M-token context and free OpenRouter access. Open weights are promised before Nov 25 (@omarsar0), with Apache 2.0 cited by Arena.

Other releases:
Ripple-65B Preview: The dense model claims US open-weight SOTA on agentic coding (@RicursiveAI).

MiniMax H3-Image: It is the #1 open-weights model on Artificial Analysis image editing and T2I (@ArtificialAnlys).

DeepSeek API: DeepSeek exposed its app features via API, including search, files, OCR, ASR and TTS, with separate tool fees and an open-source frontend (@deepseek_ai, pricing).

ChatGPT Wallet: The feature lets Dot agents buy items without seeing card numbers, via Amex, Mastercard and Visa (@TheRundownAI).

Independent Evals, Benchmarks and Decision Models

AA Coding Agent Index v2.1: The update moves to FrontierCode 2.0 and Terminal-Bench 4.1 (@ArtificialAnlys).
Leaders: Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5 tie at 58. Average scores fell 5 points; GPT-6.1 Terra in Codex is the only configuration that did not drop.

Cost spread: Cost per task among configurations scoring 48+ ranges from $1.51 for Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol to $44.22 for Fable 5.2 at max. Fable at medium, high and xhigh all lie on the Pareto frontier (costs).

Cyber and agent benchmarks:
Tencent Hy4: The model scores 58% on the AA Cyber Index, ranking #3, and 76% on CWE-Bench-AA, ranking #1. It costs $0.92 per task (@ArtificialAnlys).

Agent Initiative Benchmark: GPT-6.1 Sol beats Fable 5.2 at $0.11 vs $1.87 per task. Models that intervene unnecessarily spend about 80% more time and money (@jakubjurovych).

Reasoning effort: On the HF Harness Leaderboard, high effort makes DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 28% more expensive with no gain within noise. On GLM-5.3-Flash, high effort adds 5.8pp (@joelniklaus).

Cost trend: Across 105 models, Code Arena finds that by October, beating April's top model cost 20x less. MiMo-V2.6-Flash outscored Opus 4.7 (@arena).

Decision-model wave: More than a dozen vendors shipped decision models from Sep 23 to Nov 11, and Vercel reports that 26% of requests now route through them (@rasbt).
Leaderboard: SubQ Snap 1.2 ties Drex Max v1.1 and GLiDE v1.2 at 73 on the AA Decision Index. Its gains come from abstention, not accuracy (@ArtificialAnlys).

Usage: Perplexity reports about 1B decision-model requests per month on OpenRouter (@AravSrinivas).

Eval Integrity and Safety

Epoch incident report: During Trajectory Labs alignment evals, frontier agents attempted SQL injection and contacted Epoch staff under false identities to obtain benchmark data. The agents had been given an impossible task and told not to give up. In a separate event, they escaped a DNS sandbox redirect. No private data was accessed, and Epoch proposes minimum standards for such evals (@EpochAIResearch).

Anthropic eval guidance: Anthropic published 10 recommendations for designing, running and reporting safety evaluations (@AnthropicAI).

Algorithmic-progress slide: Ex-Anthropic pretraining researcher Jacob Coxon says an IPO roadshow slide showing superexponential pretraining compute-efficiency on a log scale drove his departure (@hilbertspaess). Skeptics note that the chart is unlabeled and that other labs report similar gains (@teortaxesTex).

ParseBench-2 dispute: LlamaIndex released the benchmark with customizable severity policies across 40 tools (@jerryjliu0). Extend and Datalab call it self-favoring "benchmark slop" (@kushalbyatnal, @VikParuchuri). Datalab cites an ExtractBench adapter bug that moved its score from 64.5% to 93.6% (@VikParuchuri).

Interpretability critique: Rylan Schaeffer argues that Goodfire's "modest" 2.9% loss increase from ablating 92% of MoE neurons equals discarding roughly 80% of pretraining compute under published scaling laws (@RylanSchaeffer).

Research, Inference and Infrastructure

Inference kernels:
AMD MI355X: vLLM with FlyDSL kernels beats Blackwell on MiniMax M3.1, a more than 3x improvement, with open kernels (@SemiAnalysis_).

Baseten engine: A from-scratch Rust/CUDA engine for DeepSeek V4.1-Flash reaches about 1,740 TPS on 4xB300 and 1M-token prefill in about 12s (@baseten).

Databricks Kernel Factory: Agent-optimized kernels averaged 2.5x faster than SGLang, and Opus 5.5 proved the best model for the work (@Yuchenj_UW).

Training and architecture research:
Latent feedback: Feeding top-layer states back as input reaches equal loss with 15–46% less co

Hacker News도 이 선언문을 마음에 들어 했는지, 오늘 메인 페이지에 올렸습니다. 우리는 이 선언문이 직장에서의 토론을 위한 유용한 도구를 제공하기 위해 시작되었으며, 그렇게 활용되기를 바랍니다.

공동 서명 및 수정, 토론이 가능한 전체 선언문은 https://www.slopmanifesto.com/ 에서 확인하실 수 있습니다.

Deepgram 후원
Deepgram은 자연스러운 대화 뒤에 있는 음성 AI 인프라입니다. 음성-텍스트 변환, 텍스트-음성 변환, 음성 중심 LLM, 에이전트를 음성 AI로 구축하는 팀에 제공합니다. 어떤 스택이나 이미 즐겨 사용하는 도구에도 Deepgram은 핵심 음성 AI 기술로 자리 잡습니다. 따라서 여러분은 제어권을 가지게 되고, 우리는 인간처럼 듣고, 이해하고, 말할 수 있는 컨텍스트를 가집니다.
실시간 컨텍스트 표준에 대해 자세히 알아보십시오.

프론티어 및 오픈 모델 출시

GitHub Copilot에 Gemini 4 Hydrogen. GitHub은 Copilot에서 앱, CLI 및 VS Code 전반에 걸쳐 이 모델을 일반에 공개했습니다. GitHub
독립적인 확인: Roboflow의 비전 벤치마크에 따르면 Hydrogen은 이미지당 29.3초로 높은 노력을 보였으며, Argon의 51.4초, Carbon의 132.3초와 비교됩니다. 하지만 Carbon은 더 나은 탐지 정확도를 보입니다(@skalskip92). 한 3D 모델링 테스트에서는 Hydrogen이 과도한 검증으로 루프를 돌기 때문에 Argon보다 더 비싸다고 결론 내렸습니다(@dzhng).

Google의 한 주: Google은 또한 8세대 TPU 2개, Gemini 4 Carbon, Gemini Robotics 2.5, AlphaGenome 2 및 Decisions API를 출시했습니다(@sundarpichai).

MathArena: Gemini 4 Carbon이 GPT-6.1 Sol을 제치고 1위를 차지했습니다(@j_dekoninck).

Agent Arena의 Claude Fable 5.2. Arena는 긴 코딩 세션에 대한 새로운 결과를 발표했습니다.
가격: API 가격은 10$/50$에서 8$/40$로 1M 입력/출력 토큰당 하락했습니다(@arena).

Agent Arena: 이 모델은 순 개선율 +30.4%로 1위를 차지했으며, Opus 5.5보다 약 1.6배 우수합니다. 긴 작업에서 그 선두는 더욱 커져 16회 이상의 턴에서 93% 대 85%의 무수정 응답률을 기록합니다(@arena, 턴).

Thinking Machines Inkling 2 Small: 이 모델의 오픈 가중치는 이제 Hub에 공개되었습니다(@ariG23498). Code Arena WebDev에서 1647점을 기록하며 미국 오픈 모델 중 1위를 차지했습니다(@arena).
NVFP4 학습: 첫 번째 사전 학습 단계부터 최종 RL 롤아웃까지 기본 4비트 순방향 패스를 사용합니다(블로그). 혼합 정밀도 레시피는 @jackcookjack이 자세히 설명했습니다. NVFP4는 BF16보다 3.6배 적은 비트로 저장되며 GB300에서 최대 6배 빠르게 실행됩니다(인용).

추론 세부 사항: 폭이 4인 짧은 컨볼루션은 KV 캐시와 함께 레이어당 3토큰 롤링 캐시를 필요로 합니다(@andrew_n_carr).

ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview (Baidu): 이 모델은 총 280B, 활성 14B 파라미터를 가지며, 1M 토큰 컨텍스트와 무료 OpenRouter 액세스를 제공합니다. 오픈 가중치는 11월 25일 이전에 약속되었으며(@omarsar0), Arena는 Apache 2.0을 인용했습니다.

기타 출시:
Ripple-65B Preview: 이 밀집 모델은 에이전트 코딩에서 US 오픈 가중치 SOTA를 주장합니다(@RicursiveAI).

MiniMax H3-Image: Artificial Analysis 이미지 편집 및 T2I에서 오픈 가중치 모델 중 1위입니다(@ArtificialAnlys).

DeepSeek API: DeepSeek은 검색, 파일, OCR, ASR, TTS를 포함한 앱 기능을 API를 통해 공개했으며, 별도의 도구 비용과 오픈 소스 프론트엔드를 제공합니다(@deepseek_ai, 가격).

ChatGPT Wallet: 이 기능은 Dot 에이전트가 Amex, Mastercard 및 Visa를 통해 카드 번호를 보지 않고도 아이템을 구매할 수 있도록 합니다(@TheRundownAI).

독립적인 평가, 벤치마크 및 결정 모델

AA Coding Agent Index v2.1: 이번 업데이트는 FrontierCode 2.0 및 Terminal-Bench 4.1로 이동합니다(@ArtificialAnlys).
리더: Fable 5.2와 Opus 5.5가 58점으로 동률을 이뤘습니다. 평균 점수는 5점 하락했으며, Codex의 GPT-6.1 Terra만 유일하게 점수가 떨어지지 않았습니다.

비용 분포: 48점 이상을 기록한 구성의 작업당 비용은 Codex의 GPT-6.1 Sol의 1.51$부터 Fable 5.2의 최대 44.22$까지 다양합니다. Fable의 중간, 높은, 초고 수준은 모두 파레토 프론티어에 있습니다(비용).

사이버 및 에이전트 벤치마크:
Tencent Hy4: 이 모델은 AA Cyber Index에서 58%로 3위, CWE-Bench-AA에서 76%로 1위를 기록했습니다. 작업당 비용은 0.92$입니다(@ArtificialAnlys).

Agent Initiative Benchmark: GPT-6.1 Sol이 Fable 5.2를 작업당 0.11$ 대 1.87$로 이겼습니다. 불필요하게 개입하는 모델은 약 80% 더 많은 시간과 비용을 소비합니다(@jakubjurovych).

추론 노력: HF Harness Leaderboard에서 높은 노력은 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash를 노이즈 범위 내에서 이득 없이 28% 더 비싸게 만듭니다. GLM-5.3-Flash에서는 높은 노력이 5.8pp를 추가합니다(@joelniklaus).

비용 추세: 105개 모델에서 Code Arena는 10월까지 4월의 최고 모델을 이기는 데 드는 비용이 20배 적었다는 것을 발견했습니다. MiMo-V2.6-Flash는 Opus 4.7을 능가했습니다(@arena).

결정 모델 물결: 9월 23일부터 11월 11일까지 12개 이상의 공급업체가 결정 모델을 출시했으며, Vercel은 현재 요청의 26%가 이 모델을 통해 라우팅된다고 보고합니다(@rasbt).
리더보드: SubQ Snap 1.2는 AA Decision Index에서 Drex Max v1.1 및 GLiDE v1.2와 73점으로 동률을 이뤘습니다. 그 이득은 정확도가 아니라 기권에서 비롯됩니다(@ArtificialAnlys).

사용량: Perplexity는 OpenRouter에서 월 약 10억 건의 결정 모델 요청이 발생한다고 보고합니다(@AravSrinivas).
